sentences.text: Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This is petitioners' appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of Nagaraj in a motor vehicle accident dated 04.08.2013.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. Petitioners are the wife and parents of deceased-Nagaraj.

It is the case of the petitioners that on 04.08.2013 at about 3-30 p.m., on Sindhanur-Raichur road, near Raghvendra rice mill, Muchal camp, in front of the Kummar Rambabu, respondent No.1 being the driver of NEKRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-37/F-366 ('offending vehicle' for short), came in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result of the accident, he sustained injuries and died on the spot.
As the owner and internal insurer respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation.
5. Respondent No.1 has remained ex parte.
6. Respondent No.2 has filed written statement denying the age, occupation, income of the deceased and also that petitioners were dependent on him and prays to dismiss the petition.
7. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.
8. Petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and Exs.P.1 to 6 are marked.
9. Respondent No.1 is examined as RW.1.
No documents are marked.

10. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.10,41,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

sentences.text:
The details of the compensation granted are as under:
 Sl. Head Amount  awarded  No.
 1. Loss of dependency Rs.8,16,000/-

2 . Loss of consortium Rs.1,00,000/-
 3. Loss of love and affection Rs.50,000/-
 4. Loss of estate Rs.50,000/-
 5. Funeral expenses Rs.25,000/-
12. Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
13. During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the notional income considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.
14. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

15. Heard arguments and perused the records.
16.

Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, Nagaraj died due to the injuries sustained in the said accident has attained finality.
17. Based on the post mortem report, the Tribunal has rightly taken the age of deceased as 26 years and 17 as the multiplier.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal is justified in considering the income of notional basis.
Since the accident is of the year 2013, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.7,000/- p.m. instead of Rs.6,000/- p.m.
However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects.

Since the deceased was below 40 years, 40% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1, (Magma's case).

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1

sentences.text: Therefore, the income is required to be taken at Rs.9,800/-.
Since there are three dependents, 1/3rd deducted towards his personal and living expenses is correct.
With these components, loss of dependency is Rs.9,800 x 12 x 17 x 2/3 = 13,32,800/-.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.13,32,800/- as against Rs.8,16,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

As wife and parents of the deceased, petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e., Rs.1,20,000/- under the head loss of consortium as against Rs.1,00,000/-
granted by the Tribunal.
Separate compensation granted in a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head loss of love and affection is disallowed.

19. As per the National Insurance Company Limited V. Pranay Sethi and others2 (Pranay Sethi's case) and Magma cases, when substantial compensation is granted under the head loss of dependency, under the conventional heads, the petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.15,000/- each under the head loss to estate and funeral expenses.

sentences.text: Hence, compensation under the head loss to estate and funeral expenses (which includes transportation charges) is reduced to Rs.15,000/- each.

20. Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.14,82,800/- as against (2017) 16 SCC 680 Rs.10,41,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:
Sl. Heads Amount Amount No. awarded by awarded by  the Tribunal this Court  1. Loss of dependency Rs.8,16,000/- Rs.13,32,800/-

2 . Loss of consortium Rs.1,00,000/- Rs.1,20,000/-
 3. Loss of love and Rs.50,000/- Disallowed  affection  4. Loss of estate Rs.50,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 5. Funeral expenses Rs.25,000/- Rs.15,000/-

To this extent, the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
a. Appeal is allowed in part.
b. Appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.14,82,800/- together with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.10,41,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

c. Respondent No.2/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order together with interest at 6%
p.a. (minus the compensation already paid/deposited).
d. Vide order dated 11.12.2018, the petitioners are not entitled to interest for delay of 550 days on the enhanced compensation.
e. Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
